newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: 1,700 Turkish Kurds on move in Iraq, UN says.
newsitem.headline: 1,700 Turkish Kurds on move in Iraq, UN says.

text.p: More than 1,700 Turkish Kurds have left a troubled refugee camp of 15,000 in northern Iraq in recent days, the United Nations refugee agency said on Tuesday.

The U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees in January withdrew from Atrush camp, which Turkey says is a base for guerrillas of the independence-seeking Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK), saying Kurdish rebels among the refugees were blocking its aid work.

The agency, which said it could only provide aid to the Kurds if they left Atrush, encouraged the refugees to move to two temporary transit sites -- Muqibla and Balkus -- set up to allow them to freely decide their destination in smaller groups.
But 1,319 Turkish Kurd refugees from the camp have shown up in Ain Sufni, on the edge of the Iraqi government controlled area, where they have been registered, a UNHCR spokesman said.
Another 392 Turkish Kurd refugees left Atrush on Monday and are resettling in villages around Dohuk, including Khanki, an agency spokeswoman said.
"There is an outflow," she told Reuters.

UNHCR spokesman Kris Janowski, speaking at a news briefing in Geneva, said: "We received reports over the weekend that some 1,300 Kurdish refugees have left Atrush camp and settled in Ain Sufni, near the Iraqi government controlled area.
"We're not quite sure whether it is government-controlled. It is actually right on the edge," he added.
"The fact that they moved that way means they are not particularly inclined to move toward Turkey," he told reporters.
The refugee agency and World Food Programme were delivering food, water, medicine, tents and kerosene to the newly displaced.

UNHCR pulled out of Atrush on January 21, acknowledging the presence of PKK rebels in the camp, to whom it refers as activists, after repeated calls from Turkey for the separation of rebels from refugees and the closure of the camp.

Atrush, 60 km (40 miles) from the Turkish border, was set up in 1994 for Kurds fleeing into northern Iraq from south-east Turkey, where villagers are caught in the middle of a guerrilla war between Turkish troops and the PKK. More than 21,000 people have died in the 12-year-old conflict.
